title: Female borrowers who mention starting their business with their own savings may fund faster.
Male borrowers who focus on a single crop rather than multiple crops may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention general biological benefits of inputs may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who provide specific details about children or family composition may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention a specific dream of buying land to build a structure may fund faster.
Female borrowers who combine business goals with educational goals fund faster than those mentioning education alone.
Male borrowers who specify exact asset quantities, such as plot size or plant count, fund faster.
Female borrowers who use aspirational language may fund faster than those who focus on quantitative operational details.
Female borrowers who use promotional language, such as describing themselves as 'deserving,' may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention spouse's employment or family support may fund faster.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention the goal of building savings fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention a history of successful loans from NWTF fund faster.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that include specific monthly income figures predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Mentioning a history of successful loan repayments has opposite effects on funding speed by gender.
